pairs.why: Both swap the real card's soft, dark gradient with faint rays and a few bubbles for a hard radial sunburst with a glow, so my vector gives no reason to choose.
A's tone-on-tone pi pattern and warm yellow field are a little quieter and closer to the real card, while B adds a brighter white glow around the hero.
B's wavy green bands and ground plane are slightly darker and quieter, which fits the real card's muted backdrop; A's lime is brighter.
A has a few large pebbles like the real card's three, while B scatters tiny ones and its rays are softer and paler than the real card's.
A keeps the plain wide vertical stripes, as the real card does. B adds an invented floor ledge with a shadow line.
A's environment is a few large shapes (tree, path, sparse bushes), like the real card. B has more bushes and clutter, and its path runs behind the table.
A is the same plain striped wall as the real card; B adds a ledge and floor shadow that the real card does not have.
B's green bands and ground are slightly darker and quieter, closer to the real card than A's bright lime, so my vector gives only a weak preference.
